India's FTAs offer access to $85 trn global market: Piyush Goyal
content:
India's existing free trade agreements provide access to an $85 trillion global market, covering about two-thirds of the world economy, Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said. 
Urging businesses to leverage these opportunities, he invited global investors to explore India's manufacturing, research, technology and innovation sectors at the 31st CII Partnership Summit.

title: USDA cuts global cotton output forecast to 117.48 mn bales
content:
USDA has cut its global cotton production forecast for 2026-27 by 470,000 bales to 117.48 million bales, citing smaller crops in India, the US, Turkiye and Argentina.
Global supplies, consumption and ending stocks were also lowered, while exports edged up to 44.82 million bales.
India's output was cut to 23.50 million bales; China and Australia were raised, and Bangladesh demand was reduced.

title: US cotton futures fall for third session amid stronger dollar
content:
US cotton futures settled marginally lower for a third session as a stronger dollar, fund rollovers and limited direction from USDA data kept trading range-bound.
December 2026 fell 0.22 per cent to 78.52 cents per pound, while March 2027 eased 0.15 per cent to 82.39 cents.
USDA cut 2026-27 global output to 117.48 million bales but also lowered consumption to 122.7 million bales.

title: North India cotton yarn sees sluggishness, prices stable
content:
North India’s cotton yarn market remained sluggish after Diwali, with Ludhiana and Delhi prices steady amid limited buying and slow factory restarts.
Traders expect demand to improve as textile production normalises and winter clothing consumption rises.
Panipat’s recycled yarn market stayed steady, while cotton gained ₹40–50 per maund on restricted arrivals and better buying.

title: Japan's Mizuno reports 9.9% H1 sales growth, retains FY27 outlook
content:
Japanese sporting goods company Mizuno Corporation reported record first-half FY27 results, with net sales rising 9.9 per cent to ~$871.96 million and operating profit increasing 22.1 per cent. 
Growth was driven by strong demand for Football, Golf, Running and Sportstyle products, particularly in Europe and the Americas. 
The company maintained its full-year forecast, targeting 8.1 per cent sales growth.

title: Canada's 14-year tariff plan: Can Indonesia win more apparel orders?
content:
Indonesia’s apparel share in Canada rose to 3.35 per cent in January-August 2026 as its shipments slipped 0.6 per cent while Canada’s total apparel imports fell 7.3 per cent.
TexPro says knitted imports from Indonesia grew 6.6 per cent to $132.94 million, while woven apparel dropped 8.1 per cent to $109.52 million.
CEPA starts on December 1, 2026, with duty cuts and fabric-origin flexibility.

title: Bangladesh's RMG exports to EU rise 2.79% in July-October
content:
Bangladesh's ready-made garment exports to the EU rose 2.79 per cent year-on-year to $6.43 billion in July-October of fiscal 2026-27, EPB data showed.
Spain led with $1.448 billion and Germany followed with $1.439 billion; the top five EU markets accounted for two-thirds of exports.
October exports to the bloc increased 1.10 per cent to $1.53 billion.

title: On Holding keeps its premium edge as apparel and running surge
content:
Swiss sportswear brand On Holding reported Q3 sales up 17.2 per cent to CHF 931.4 million, with earnings per share rising to CHF 0.48.
Growth spanned all regions, channels and product categories; Asia Pacific led regional gains, while direct-to-consumer sales rose 25 per cent.

title: US' Levi Strauss names Jeannie Renné-Malone as sustainability chief
content:
Levi Strauss & Co. has named Jeannie Renné-Malone as vice-president, chief sustainability officer, effective December 1, to lead its global Sustainability team.
She will also join the Supply Chain Leadership Team as LS&Co. works on sustainability goals spanning its supply chain, products and communities.
Renné-Malone was most recently VP, global head of sustainability at VF Corporation.
